Photo by Chesnot/Getty Images
Bitcoin had been on an uptrend since April 12 when it hit a recent low of $6,850. Tom Lee, Head of Research at Fundstrat, had postulated that at least part of the weakness in Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies in March and the first two weeks of April had been due to &l;a href=&q;http://www.forbes.com/sites/chuckjones/2018/04/22/bitcoin-continues-rebounding-after-april-17-tax-day/&q;&g;investors selling them to raise cash to pay for 2017 gains&l;/a&g;.
It got as high as $9,950 on Saturday, May 5, but later in the day it started moving lower which seemed to be about the same time that Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger at the Berkshire Hathaway&a;rsquo;s shareholder meeting &l;a href=&q;http://www.forbes.com/sites/chuckjones/2018/05/07/warren-buffett-stalls-bitcoins-advance-just-short-of-10000/&q;&g;made multiple statements denigrating it&l;/a&g;. It fell to $9,300 last Sunday and essentially traded between $9,000 to $9,400 until Thursday evening. On Friday it broke down and fell to $8,300.
&l;img class=&q;size-full wp-image-11952&q; src=&q;http://blogs-images.forbes.com/chuckjones/files/2018/05/BITCOIN-PRICE-CHART-APRIL-7-2018-TO-MAY-11-2018.jpg?width=960&q; alt=&q;Bitcoin price chart since April 7&q; data-height=&q;464&q; data-width=&q;1177&q;&g; Bitcoin price chart since April 7
&l;p class=&q;tweet_line&q;&g;There is a major cryptocurrency conference in New York City next week and Lee believes that while there could be negative news flow from the conference regarding regulations, the weakness of Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies since the beginning of the year make them poised for a post-conference rebound.
&l;strong&g;Korea and Mt. Gox impacted Bitcoin on Friday&l;/strong&g;
The most recent downdraft seems to have been caused by Korea&a;rsquo;s Financial Supervisory Commission visiting Upbit, the country&a;rsquo;s largest cryptocurrency exchange. &l;a href=&q;https://cointelegraph.com/news/s-koreas-largest-crypto-exchange-upbit-investigated-by-police-markets-react&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;Cointelegraph.com reported&l;/a&g; from the Korean news outlet &l;a href=&q;http://news.chosun.com/site/data/html_dir/2018/05/11/2018051101843.html&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;Chosun&l;/a&g;, that the regulators were investigating Upbit for faking balance sheets and deceiving customers.
Upbit was the fourth largest worldwide cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume per &l;a href=&q;https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/volume/24-hour/&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;coinmarketcap.com&l;/a&g;. However, per &l;a href=&q;http://data.bitcoinity.org/markets/volume/30d?c=c&a;amp;r=day&a;amp;t=b&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;bitcoinity.org&l;/a&g; the Korean Won accounted for less than 2% of Bitcoin&a;rsquo;s total trading volume by currency over the past 30 days, so this by itself shouldn&a;rsquo;t have a large impact on Bitcoin.
CCN.com reported that Mt. Gox was positioning to liquidate 8,200 Bitcoins to pay off previous investors. This number of Bitcoins represents about 10% of the cryptocurreny&a;rsquo;s past two weeks daily trading volume. If the selling is spread over multiple days &l;a href=&q;http://www.forbes.com/sites/chuckjones/2018/03/12/blaming-mt-gox-for-bitcoins-recent-price-drop-just-doesnt-compute/&q;&g;it shouldn&a;rsquo;t have much of an impact&l;/a&g;, besides a psychological one.
&l;!–nextpage–&g;
&a;nbsp;
&l;strong&g;Cryptocurrency and Blockchain conference in New York City next week&l;/strong&g;
Consensus 2018 is a three day conference on cryptocurrencies and Blockchain being held in New York City starting on Monday next week. In just four years it has become one of the largest crypto conferences in the world and is &l;a href=&q;https://www.coindesk.com/events/consensus-2018/&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;hosted by CoinDesk&l;/a&g;.
From the conference website it says the conference will &a;ldquo;feature 250+ speakers and 4,000+ attendees from the leading industry startups, investors, financial institutions, enterprise tech leaders, and academic and policy groups who are building the foundations of the blockchain and digital currency economy.&a;rdquo; Its attendance has exploded. Starting from three years ago it should grow by at least 10x and may push 20x. The number of attendees by year is:
&l;/p&g;&l;ul&g;&l;li&g;2015 400&l;/li&g;
&l;li&g;2016 1,400&l;/li&g;
&l;li&g;2017 2,700&l;/li&g;
&l;li&g;2018 4,000 plus and it could exceed 7,000&l;/li&g;
&l;/ul&g;&l;strong&g;Tom Lee at Fundstrat believes this conference could help Bitcoin rebound&l;/strong&g;
While it is only three data points, Lee believes there is a pattern of Bitcoin moving higher during and after the conference . From a week prior to the end of the conferences, Bitcoin has rallied 10% to 69% and after two months it has increased 78% to 138%. Since Bitcoin is down year to date and with the large increase in attendance, Lee believes Bitcoin is primed to move higher.
&l;img class=&q;size-full wp-image-11953&q; src=&q;http://blogs-images.forbes.com/chuckjones/files/2018/05/Bitcoin-Tom-Lee-Fundstrat-Consensus-cryptocurrency-conference-price-chart.jpg?width=960&q; alt=&q;Bitcoin price moves from past and current Consensus conferences&q; data-height=&q;629&q; data-width=&q;1160&q;&g; Bitcoin price moves from past and current Consensus conferences
Lee has also developed indexes of other cryptocurrencies, one of which is the FS CryptoFX 250. It tracks the 51&l;sup&g;st&l;/sup&g; to 300&l;sup&g;th&l;/sup&g; largest cryptocurrencies based on market cap and liquidity. Over the same timeframe of one week prior to the Consensus conferences until their end, this index has increased 9% to 176%. At two months post conference, the index has risen 56% to 552%.
